title: Data Handling
description: Class 6 IMO — Data handling: collecting and organising data with tally marks, scaled pictographs, bar graphs and double bar graphs, and finding the mean (average).

topics.title: Tally Marks & Pictographs
topics.concept: Data can be recorded with tally marks in groups of five. A pictograph shows data with pictures, where one picture stands for a fixed number (the scale). If 1 picture = 10, then 4 pictures mean 40.

examples.problem: On a pictograph 1 symbol = 10 books. How many books do 4 symbols show?
How many does one full tally group stand for?

recap: Tally marks group counts in fives.
Pictograph: one picture stands for a fixed number (the scale).

quiz.q: On a pictograph 1 picture = 5 apples. How many apples do 6 pictures show?
Two full tally groups stand for ___ ?

topics.title: Bar Graphs & Double Bar Graphs
topics.concept: A bar graph shows data with bars whose heights give the values. A double bar graph shows two sets of data side by side so they can be compared — for example, the marks of two students.

examples.problem: What does a double bar graph let us do?
examples.solution: Compare two sets of data side by side.

examples.problem: If one bar is 20 and another is 15, what is the difference?

recap: Bar heights give the values; the tallest shows the most.
A double bar graph compares two sets of data.

quiz.q: Bar A is 20 and bar B is 15. What is the difference?
A double bar graph is used to compare ___ ?
quiz.explanation: It compares two sets of data.

topics.title: Mean (Average)
topics.concept:
Four Measures of Central Tendency:

MeasureDefinitionHow to FindExample: 2,4,6,8,10
MeanAverageSum ÷ Count(2+4+6+8+10)/5 = 6
MedianMiddle valueOrder, find middle2,4,6,8,10 → 6
ModeMost frequentFind most commonNo mode (all appear once)
RangeSpreadMax - Min10 - 2 = 8

When to Use Each:

MeasureBest Used When
MeanData is symmetrical, no outliers
MedianData has outliers (very high/low values)
ModeData has repeating values (favorite colors)
RangeWant to know spread of data
MEAN AS "BALANCE POINT":

    Data: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10
    
    <----|----|----|----|----|---->
         2    4    6    8    10
              ↑    ↑
              ←──┼──→
         Left sum = Right sum
         (2+4=6, 8+10=18) Not equal? Actually mean=6 balances:
         Deviations: -4, -2, 0, +2, +4 → sum of deviations=0


MEDIAN VISUAL:

    Odd count (5 numbers):
    2, 4, 6, 8, 10 → median = 6 (3rd number)
    
    Even count (6 numbers):
    2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 → median = (6+8)/2 = 7


MODE VISUAL:

    Data: 3, 5, 5, 7, 7, 7, 9
    
    Frequency:
    9│        ■
    8│        
    7│     ■  ■  ■
    6│        
    5│  ■  ■  ■
    4│        
    3│  ■
    └──────────────
       3  5  7  9
        
    Mode = 7 (appears 3 times)


RANGE VISUAL:

    Data: 15, 22, 31, 18, 45
    
    Min = 15, Max = 45
    Range = 45 - 15 = 30
    
    <─── Range = 30 ───→
    ├─────┼─────────────┤
    15                  45

examples.problem: Find mean, median, mode, and range of: 5, 8, 12, 8, 7
examples.solution:
• Mean = (5+8+12+8+7)/5 = 40/5 = 8
  • Order: 5,7,8,8,12 → median = 8
  • Mode = 8 (appears twice)
  • Range = 12 - 5 = 7
  • Answer: Mean=8, Median=8, Mode=8, Range=7

• Order: 15,18,20,22,25,30
  • Even count: middle two are 20 and 22
  • Median = (20+22)/2 = 21
  • Answer: 21

• 2 appears twice, 3 appears twice
  • Two modes = bimodal
  • Answer: 2 and 3

recap: Mean = sum of values ÷ number of values.
The mean is also called the average.
Outliers affect mean more than median
